response.answer:
Parasite-clearance half-life is usually more informative because it is derived from the slope of the post-treatment decline in parasitaemia, so it captures subtle slowing of clearance that appears long before blood smears become negative. By contrast, time to microscopy negativity is strongly censored by assay detection limits, starting parasitaemia, sampling frequency, and stage structure, so it is a coarse endpoint that mixes drug effect with host and measurement factors.

Thus the half-life is an emergent population-level phenotype of parasite susceptibility plus host and treatment context, not an intrinsic single-parameter kill constant.
